Samir/Markus —

Thanks for the redlines. High-level legal notes:
1) 99.95% is aggressive given our current multi-tenant hosted footprint; to accept this contractually we need to add service fencing (Dedicated) plus operational review prerequisites.
2) The rollback clause needs to be scoped to "material degradation of customer-facing latency or correctness" and should include objective metrics and an agreed evaluation window (we suggest 24 hours post-deploy) to avoid churn-prone flips.
3) Credit calculation: propose caps and a non-cumulative remedy to limit financial exposure; we can offer an additive credit schedule up to 100% of one month's committed value in extreme cases.
4) Maintenance: legal can accept a monthly cap but recommends straightforward wording around "scheduled maintenance" vs "emergency maintenance" and notification windows.

I'll draft specific redline language for the MSA and Order Form. Laura/dev — please provide operational constraints (max maintenance duration, typical P1 remediation processes) so I can write defensible language.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Operational facts to inform legal redlines:

- We can add an explicit blackout exception: customers may lock a one-week quarterly peak window with 14 days' advance notice.
